subsections.title: Nickname & PIN
subsections.html:
Your nickname is your account. It labels your forum posts and lets your attempts and progress follow you to other devices. No email, phone number or real name is involved, and your stats stay private.

Getting one

The first time you press Start, a Getting Started! screen explains this and then asks for a nickname (no spaces, up to 40 characters). You get a 5-digit PIN. Keep it somewhere safe: the app can't recover it.

A name typed into the Forum's name box is claimed the same way when you send your first message.

Managing it

WhereControls
Stats, the ⚙︎ next to your nameChange nickname · Your PIN · Exit
Forum, above the message boxChange · PIN · Exit
  • Change keeps your PIN (Stats asks you to type it). The avatar is made anew from the new name, and your past messages show the new name.
  • Your PIN shows the PIN this device remembers. Anyone who has it can take over your nickname.
  • Exit signs out this device only. The nickname stays yours and other devices stay signed in. Your attempts and progress stay on the server; this device's copies are removed.

On another device

Enter the same nickname and its PIN, either when you start a quiz or through Already claimed a nickname on another device? under the Forum's name box. Everything synced comes back: see Cross-device sync.

subsections.title: Random quiz
subsections.html:
Random {{quizSize}} draws {{quizSize}} problems at random and times you, like a real quiz. Every checked attempt is saved to your Stats.

SwitchDraws from
📝 Single Setthe selected set
📚 Sets 1–N{{cumulativePrev}} problems from all earlier sets together and {{cumulativeCurrent}} from the selected one, mixed. From Set #2 on.

The Problem pool filter under the problems narrows what can be drawn.

Taking it

  • Type each answer in its box (how to write them). Enter moves to the next box, and on the last one it checks the quiz. 📋 Show hint (units & numbers) opens a cheat sheet.
  • A clock counts up in the bottom-right corner. The site goes full screen when the quiz starts and leaves it when your score shows; in full screen the top bar shows the time and battery.
  • Check answers grades everything at once. New quiz ↺ draws a fresh set. An attempt you never check isn't saved.

After checking

Answer =

A checked card: the right value without its unit. 💬 shows how many messages the problem's thread has.
  • Every card is marked correct, partly correct or wrong; a wrong one shows the expected value. 📘 See solution appears where a worked solution exists, and 💬 opens the problem's forum thread. Neither is there before you check.
  • The result panel shows your score, the time taken and a box per problem. In a Sets 1–N attempt, P⇄Q switches the boxes between problem and set numbers.
  • Last attempts lists your five latest attempts (a box opens that problem's thread), and Topics in this attempt shows how you do on those topics overall. See full stats → opens Stats.

Settings → Study can hide the clock, submit after 50 minutes, turn off full screen, hide topics until the score shows, and start on the latest set or on Sets 1–N.

subsections.title: Entering answers & scoring
subsections.html:
Type the whole answer in one box: the number, then its unit, like 9.81 m/s^2. A problem without a unit takes just the number. While you type, a box under the field shows how your answer is read, or what is wrong with it. A plain number shows nothing there, so a missing unit is never hinted at.

Try it: the stored answer here is 9.81 m/s^2.
Answer =
Checked live by the site's own checker. Try 9.81, 9.8 N/kg or 9.81 m*s^-2.

Numbers

  • Decimals take a period: 3.14, -0.5. A comma (3,14) isn't accepted.
  • Powers of ten: 1.6e-19, 2.998E8, 5*10^3, 10^-4. Not 1.6x10^5.
  • Simple arithmetic with pi and e: 3/4, 2*pi, (1+2)/3. No functions such as sqrt().
  • The value is checked with a tolerance of about 1%, so ordinary rounding is fine.

Units

WriteFor
N mmultiplying: a space
N/C, kg m/s^2, J/(kg K)dividing: one slash
m^2, s^-1, s^(-1), m²powers
  • Units are case-sensitive. These are invalid and score 0, as in Moodle: N*m (use a space), m m (write m^2), m/s/s (one slash only), m/s^(2) (brackets only around a negative power).
  • Equivalent SI units count: J = N m = kg m^2/s^2, V/m = N/C, Wb = V s = T m^2, Hz = s^-1. rad on its own counts as no unit.
  • Units outside SI only match themselves and their own prefixes: km/h is not m/s, L is not m^3, eV is not J.

SI prefixes

Every SI unit in the course (m, s, g, A, K, mol, N, J, W, Pa, Hz, C, V, Ohm/Ω, F, T, Wb, H) takes a prefix written right before it: mA, kOhm, mg, ns. It is converted to the stored answer's unit. For micro, u, mc or mk work too.

Animations

subsections.title: Posting & identity
subsections.html:
Messages go out under your nickname. On a device without one, type a name and send: it's claimed on your first message and you get its PIN. If someone already has that name, you're asked for its PIN.

Start typing…
The avatars for the users are generated procedurally based on the nickname, try it out here!

Where a message goes

The picker above the box sets the thread: 🌐 Global, a quiz, or one of its problems. A quiz with no problem picked goes to that quiz's general thread. Opened from a problem's 💬 button, the forum posts to that problem.

Writing

  • $\mathrm{La\TeX}$ works: see Writing LaTeX in messages.
  • Type @ to tag someone; the list always offers @gemini first. Tap a tagged name to see that person's avatar and message count.
  • ↩ on a message replies to it with a short quote. ✎ on your own message edits its text or moves it to another thread, at any time; edited messages show (ed.).
  • A message holds up to 1000 characters, and there's an 8-second pause between posts.

subsections.title: Threads & alerts
subsections.html:
Every problem has its own thread. Its 💬 button sits on the problem's card in Entire Set, in a checked Random {{quizSize}} quiz and in an attempt review. The boxes in Last attempts and in Stats → Problems overview open it too.

5 messages, none unread · 2 unread · 2 unread, and one of them tags you.
  • Opened from a problem, the forum shows just that thread, with the problem's text above it, which you can fold away.
  • Otherwise Show filters the list: All, 🌐 Global, a quiz, then one of its problems. 🔍 searches every message.
  • Newest messages are on top. Older ones load as you scroll down, and when new ones arrive a pill takes you back up.
  • A pinned welcome message stays on top until you close it, or for 24 hours after you first see it.

Alerts

  • The 💬 Forum buttons count unread messages and show @ when you're tagged. Besides the one on the main screen, a floating 💬 sits at the bottom-left of other screens (not during an unchecked Random {{quizSize}} quiz); tap it again to close the forum.
  • 🔕 in the forum's header turns on notifications for tags, which arrive even with the site closed. Your browser asks first, and nothing but tags is ever sent.
  • Settings → Notifications → Go silent hides every badge and mutes these notifications.

subsections.title: Writing LaTeX in messages
subsections.html:
The forum renders $\mathrm{La\TeX}$ the same way problems do. Wrap inline math in single dollar signs, and display math (on its own centred line) in double dollar signs:

The field is $E = \frac{kq}{r^2}$, pointing radially outward.

The field is $E = \frac{kq}{r^2}$, pointing radially outward.

$$\Delta V = -\int_{a}^{b} \vec{E}\cdot \mathrm{d}\vec{l}$$

$$\Delta V = -\int_{a}^{b} \vec{E}\cdot \mathrm{d}\vec{l}$$

Not sure of the $\mathrm{La\TeX}$? The $\mathbf{\Sigma}$ button next to the message box opens an equation composer with a live preview and quick-insert buttons for fractions, integrals, sums, trig functions and Greek letters. Tick Own line for a display equation.

Or write it in words: wrap a description in single &s for inline math, or double &&s for a display equation, and it is converted into $\mathrm{La\TeX}$ before your message posts. &E equals m c squared& becomes $E = mc^2$. If the conversion fails, you can post your original text as it is instead of losing it.

Try it yourself

Type anything below and it’s wrapped in $$ $$ and typeset live underneath, so you can see exactly how an expression will look before posting it.

Edit the box above — the render below updates as you type.

subsections.title: Gemini, the forum bot
subsections.html:
Gemini is a bot that joins a thread when tagged. Mention @gemini anywhere in a message (typing @ always offers it first) and it replies a moment later. It reads the rest of the conversation and, in a problem’s thread, that problem’s text and figure.

It won’t always reply: a trivial reply to one of its own messages, or a hostile one, is ignored. There’s no limit on tagging it, but it refuses anything unrelated to physics. Its replies are screened like everyone else’s.

GeminiGlobal(ed.)Aug 9, 3:42 PM
Hi! I’m Gemini. I’m here to help you with physics — tag me with @gemini anywhere and I’ll be there faster than you can say “moment of inertia.”
Preview of Gemini replies in the forum.

subsections.title: Moderation & flags
subsections.html:
Every message, including Gemini’s replies, is screened automatically before it appears, so most disallowed content is never posted.

If something slips through, flag it with ⚑ (up to 5 flags an hour). The message and a bit of the thread around it go to an automatic review, which keeps it or removes it; there is no manual queue. Three removed messages within 24 hours ban their author from posting for 24 hours; the next bans last 48 and then 72 hours. A banner in the message box counts down the time left.

BornGlobal(ed.)Aug 9, 3:41 PM
Maxwell would tell you it’s over for you, give up!
BornGlobal(ed.)Aug 9, 3:41 PM
Maxwell would tell you it’s over for you, give up!
BornGlobal(ed.)Aug 9, 3:41 PM
This message was removed by auto-moderation after being flagged. Reason: harassment.
MaxwellGlobal(ed.)Aug 9, 3:41 PM
Maybe my demon, but not me! Keep going!
Four snapshots of how flagging plays out. The first three are the same message by Born as it moves through moderation: Gray flag, not yet flagged, the default idle state every message starts in. Yellow flag, someone flagged it and it is being auto-reviewed. Red flag, review finished and the message was removed, the body is replaced by a removal notice the same way a real deletion renders. The last one, by Maxwell, shows a different outcome: Green flag, the message was flagged, but the review found no violation, so it stays up and the flag just marks it as reviewed.

Reviewing an attempt

Review shows an attempt as it was checked: quiz, mode, date, duration and score on top, a box per problem that jumps to its card, and each card with what you typed, the points it got then and, if it was wrong, the expected value. subsections.title: What gets tracked
subsections.html:
Only Random {{quizSize}} attempts are recorded: the set, Single Set or Sets 1–N, date, duration, score, and for each problem what you typed and its points. Entire Set keeps its own progress instead: which problems you solved, missed or revealed, and what you typed.

What the server stores

DataWho sees it
A random ID for this browser, used to link it to your nickname and to count visitsnobody
Your nickname, avatar, join date and a salted hash of your PIN; the PIN itself stays on your deviceseveryone sees your nickname and avatar next to your posts
Random quiz attempts and Entire Set progressonly your own devices; others see only site-wide totals
Forum messageseveryone
A push address, if you turn on tag notificationsnobody

No email, real name or browser details are stored in the database. Settings, theme and filters never leave your browser.

Services involved

  • The data is kept by Supabase, with the primary database in Tokyo, Japan, under the Supabase Privacy Policy, its Terms of Service and its Logs & Analytics.
  • The hosting provider, Netlify, keeps standard request logs (IP address, user agent, request details, performance) for up to 30 days: see Netlify’s GDPR and CCPA statement.
  • Messages, edits and nicknames are checked by OpenAI’s moderation service. Google Gemini answers @gemini, converts &…& math and reviews flagged messages. DiceBear draws avatars from nicknames.

There’s no automatic account deletion yet. To delete yours, ask @Aoi_Kuro on Telegram.

subsections.title: Cross-device sync
subsections.html:
Every device signed in with your nickname shares the same attempts and progress. There's nothing to press: a dot next to Attempt log and in the Entire Set progress window shows the state (green: synced, grey: syncing, red: the last try failed and is retried).

SyncsHow
Random quiz attemptsSent as soon as you check; your other devices pick them up within moments. Deleting one removes it everywhere. An attempt that couldn't be sent shows not synced until it gets through.
Entire Set progressPer set, while it's open and when you leave. Devices merge instead of overwriting each other: a problem solved on either stays solved. Reset Progress resets it on all of them.

Settings, theme, day/night and filters stay in each browser. Backup moves settings by hand.

subsections.title: Offline mode & storage
subsections.html:
Go offline

Settings → Sync & Storage → 📥 Go offline (tap twice) downloads every quiz, image, worked solution and app file, then runs the site from that copy for 24 hours, blocking every server request even once you're back online. Handy for studying on the road.

While offline
Worksboth quiz modes, answer checking, solutions, Stats from this device, settings and themes
Waitsnew attempts and progress are saved here and sync when you're online again
Offthe forum and Gemini, site-wide totals, notifications, PDF and Excel export

Go back online now ends it early. If the download fails, nothing is blocked; ↻ Try again.

Without Go offline, losing the connection shows an offline page, with a physics law to read meanwhile. It reloads by itself once you're back.

Cache & storage

Button (tap twice)Does
Reset all cacheClears the attempts and Entire Set progress stored in this browser, then reloads. Nothing is deleted from the server: the next sync brings it back.
Reset prerendered $\mathrm{La\TeX}$ equationsForgets the stored equations of every quiz; Entire Set draws them again next time.
Reinstall service workerRefreshes the part of the site that stores files and works offline, then reloads. A Go offline download is kept.

Backup

⬇️ Export settings saves every setting to a file, and ⬆️ Import settings restores one, also on another device. A setting added since the backup keeps its default.

subsections.title: Themes & fonts
subsections.html:
Every screen can be recoloured two independent ways: pick one of eight built-in colour themes, or your own, from 🎨, and flip between day and night with the sun/moon switch. Any theme works in either mode, and with a forum nickname your choice follows you to your other devices. Each window below shows a theme’s night half (left) and day half (right); click one to switch to it.

Default
Default — modeled on GitHub’s own dark interface, familiar to anyone who’s stared at a diff at 2am.
Nord
Nord — the well-known arctic palette popular in code editors: cool grays with a frosty blue accent.
Sakura
Sakura — cherry-blossom pink with the roundest corners of any preset, for a softer, cozier feel.
Cyber
Cyber — neon cyberpunk glow, near-zero corner rounding, and Space Grotesk type for a sharper edge.
Forest
Forest — earthy woodland greens and browns, calm and grounded.
Solar
Solar — sunlight: a gold eclipse glow on warm near-black at night, burnt orange on cream paper by day, with generous curves.
Dusk
Dusk — violet twilight with a peach afterglow, softly rounded.
Ocean
Ocean — deep-sea navy with seafoam and coral, cool and clear.
Custom
Custom — whatever you’ve set up in the custom theme builder, previewed live from your saved settings. Click to switch to it.

Settings → Display can follow your device’s light/dark mode instead, and scale every figure with Figure size.

Fonts

IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono are the default UI pairing everywhere outside a themed override. Space Grotesk/Space Mono take over under Cyber, Quicksand under Sakura, and Bangers is reserved for the landing screen’s splash text. Problem statements and every rendered equation use STIX Two Text, a serif built for math typesetting, so formulas read like they belong in an actual physics textbook instead of a UI font stretched to do double duty.

Custom theme

The custom builder skips picking every variable by hand: set a background, text, and two accent colors separately for night and day, plus a corner-roundness slider and one of four font pairings (Plex, Grotesk, Quicksand, or all-mono). Surface panels, borders, and muted text are auto-derived by blending your background toward your text color, with a live preview before you save.

subsections.title: About the project
subsections.html:
This project started small, in June 2026, when I took PHYS 162 in the summer term. To be precise, it wasn’t even a webpage yet: I just shared a single HTML file with my peers in the group. There were no other modes besides a random set of 6 problems, no forum, no themes, no stats, no changelog, not even unit parsing (initially you just entered the number in SI with no units). Just a quick way to practice PHYS 162 without digging through a PDF.

Aoi-Kuro/impulseView on GitHub ↗
Loading live stats…

Then it grew step by step, as you can see in the changelog: solve-them-all mode (now Entire Set), a daylight switcher, $\mathrm{La\TeX}$ support, and more. Later came PHYS 161, a Moodle-style answer engine and worked solutions with step-by-step figures, each credited to its author. A lot of smaller UI work went uncovered along the way too: for instance, every time you open Entire Set mode, all the $\mathrm{La\TeX}$ expressions are pre-rendered and cached locally, so the next time you open the quiz you don’t have to wait for it.

I also tried to make the site feel like more than a dead screen that just tells you your score. Splashes, a few easter eggs, and a forum went in to make it feel alive.

Splashes from the main screen. Give it a tap!

The forum, actually, was a suggestion from a friend of mine who wasn’t even using the site, not something I’d originally planned. It grew from a simple read-only feed into a full system with nicknames, PINs, $\mathrm{La\TeX}$ support, moderation, mentions, and replies. This manual was built the same way: as a request, then built out properly rather than left as an afterthought.

Aside from learning PHYS 162, I hoped this could show what enthusiasm alone can do. I didn’t know a thing about web development, database design, or anything else you see here when I started: I only had the desire to do it. And here we are.

Whether you think you can, or you think you can’t — you’re right.

Henry Ford

subsections.title: Feedback & Contact
subsections.html:
Found a bug, a typo, or a wrong answer key on one of the problems? Message me on Telegram, @Aoi_Kuro. Small fixes like a mistake in a problem's answer key, a spelling error, or a broken formula usually go out fast; I will likely do it on the spot, so most of these get sorted the same day.

Prefer GitHub?Open an issue ↗
Loading live stats…

Bigger feature requests are welcome too: send them the same way. Nothing about this site is fixed in stone; the forum itself started as exactly this kind of suggestion. I can't promise a timeline on anything larger, since it depends on free time between coursework, but I do keep a list and go through it when I get a proper break. If enough people ask for the same thing, that moves it up.

So: small stuff gets fixed fast, big stuff gets considered and maybe built for whoever's using this site next.
